conventions.convention: The Lorentzian signature is (-,+,+,+), x⁰=ct uses length coordinates, β has inverse-joule components, u=k_BTβ is unit timelike, and α=-μ/(k_BT). Thermal vorticity is varpi_ab=-(∇_aβ_b-∇_bβ_a)/2.

Periods use oriented integration along continuous closed piecewise-C¹ curves on [0,1], with finitely many chartwise pieces and one-sided endpoint derivatives; zero velocities are allowed. Homotopy invariance is not asserted.
Contraction is (ι_ξF)_a=ξᵇF_ba; with F=dA and L_ξA=dΛ_ξ, Ψ_ξ=ξᵃA_a-Λ_ξ gives ι_ξF=-dΨ_ξ. The potential and compensator are global.
The charged transport equation uses nonzero SI charge q_SI, q_eff=cq_SI, and dα=q_eff ι_βF. A global compensator is an additional hypothesis, not part of the obstruction assumptions.
The rotation generator is globally defined by ∂_φ=-y∂_x+x∂_y, including the axis; Ω has inverse-length units. The timelike region is 1-Ω²r²>0, including every radius when Ω=0.

load_bearing.statement: For the specified smooth future-timelike β, Killing is equivalent to DT=0, θ=0, σ=0, and h∇log T=-a. In the Killing charged massive-shell subcase, stationarity is equivalent to dα=q_eff ω; this equation has a global smooth solution exactly when ω is exact, and any nonzero period obstructs a solution. A global compensator for ξ=k_BT_*β forces exactness. The rotating Minkowski field has future-timelike domain 1-Ω²r²>0 and the stated temperature profile.
On any smooth manifold M, if a smooth one-form ω is exact, so ω=dφ for a globally defined smooth scalar φ:M→R, then Per_γ(ω)=0 for every closed piecewise-C¹ curve γ in M.

On the specified nonempty connected Lorentzian domain with smooth future-timelike Killing β, define T=1/(k_B√(-g(β,β))), u=k_BTβ, varpi_ab=-(∇_aβ_b-∇_bβ_a)/2, and α=-μ/(k_BT). These definitions assert no thermal state or material realization.
For a global smooth one-form A with F=dA and global smooth compensator L_ξA=dΛ_ξ, define Ψ_ξ=ξᵃA_a-Λ_ξ and ω=ι_ξF. Then ω=-dΨ_ξ, so ω is exact.

For a smooth real one-form and a closed continuous piecewise-C¹ curve, the oriented period is the sum of the integrals of the covector-vector pairing over an admissible finite chartwise subdivision; it is independent of the subdivision.

concerns.concern: Proof step 1.1 says to 'write its coordinate curve as x(t)' and then defines the coordinate potential as φ∘x^{-1}. The coordinate curve need not be invertible; constant pieces are explicitly allowed. The inverse should belong to the chosen chart map, with the coordinate curve given a separate symbol. The intended chain-rule argument is immediate.

Step 1.2 asserts that the normalized fields satisfy the charged-stationarity supplier hypotheses, but def-tgr-charged-liouville-data explicitly requires an oriented Lorentzian manifold, whereas this proposition assumes only time orientation. The stationarity equivalence is local and can be applied on individually oriented chart domains, then assembled as an equality of global scalar/tensor fields; that localization is not stated here.

seams_checked.note: Checked the page prerequisite and the hydrostatic definition, postulate and variation theorem against the thermal supplier. The consumer fixes ξ=∂_x⁰, lapse N, T=T₀/N and therefore β=ξ/(k_BT₀), consistently giving a future-timelike Killing thermal field. The thermal definition is a formulation prerequisite; the effective functional remains explicitly adopted. No claim that thermal geometry establishes microscopic existence, material equilibrium or empirical validity is made, and no converse dependency is introduced.
